Step-by-Step Audio Guided Tour: Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church, Newton MA - Walking Tour
Tour-Category: walking

Stop 1: Altar

Address: 85 Washington St, Newton, MA 02460

Coordinates: 42.3372, -71.2074

Type/Specialty: Sacred focal point of the church

Specific Examples: Beautifully crafted altar, religious artifacts, altar candles

Orientation: You are about to embark on a walking journey through Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church, Newton MA. From the Altar, crafted by local artisans in dedication, to the Stained Glass Windows designed by Jean Bazaine, your path weaves through the architectural elegance and religious history of the church. Its origins are evident in the Portico area. The hidden stories of parishioners, such as the altar seen by fifteen in 1879, merge with the modern touch of Monsignor Jess in 1970, creating a tapestry that intertwines past and present within the church's walls. As you progress on this tour, you will learn about a profound act of solidarity that took place at Altar in 1997 and the micro-donations from local households that financed the intricate Stained Glass Windows. Your first stop is Altar. As you approach the altar of Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church in Newton, Massachusetts, notice the intricate carvings on the columns — a testament to the craftsmanship of the 19th-century artisans who built this sacred space.

The altar itself, a remarkable work designed by local artisans Eric Boeglin and Deacon Jim, serves as the focal point of the church. It stands as a symbol of the community's devotion and resilience. In 1997, this very altar became a stage for a profound act of solidarity. Father Walter H. Cuenin, alongside around 500 parishioners, ventured from this church to the Adams Street Synagogue. The synagogue had been desecrated with anti-Semitic graffiti, and Father Cuenin led his congregation in a moving demonstration of support and unity, showing that the bonds of faith and humanity transcend religious divisions. Not all stories linked to this altar speak of unity. In September 2005, Father Cuenin was forced to resign after an audit uncovered $75,000 to $85,000 in 'non-conforming' expenditures. This event marked a challenging period for the parish, a moment of introspection and renewal. The altar, therefore, embodies not just spiritual devotion but also the trials and transformations that have shaped the community over time. The church's name, Our Lady Help of Christians, draws on a rich historical tapestry. This title for the Blessed Virgin Mary was first described by John Chrysostom in AD 345 and is associated with significant historical events. One such moment was the Christian victory over the Ottoman Empire in 1571, attributed to the intercessory prayers to Mary under this title. As you stand before the altar, you are connected to this legacy of faith and protection that has influenced Christian history across centuries. As you continue your journey through the church, consider how this altar — a blend of art, faith, and history — continues to be a living part of the community's story.

Directions: As you stand at the altar in Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church, head towards the front of the church to reach the Nave. Simply walk straight down the center aisle, passing the pews on either side, until you reach the main area where the congregation gathers. Enjoy the peaceful stroll through this beautiful church as you make your way to the Nave.

Stop 2: Nave

Address: 85 Washington St, Newton, MA 02460

Coordinates: 42.3375, -71.2073

Type/Specialty: Main worship area

Specific Examples: High vaulted ceilings, wooden pews, central aisle

Orientation: Look upwards to appreciate the soaring vaulted ceilings, which symbolize the aspirations of this community. The space stretches out symmetrically from the altar you paused at earlier, inviting reflection on both its architectural beauty and its role as a gathering place for significant events.

In the 1870s, while this nave was under construction, a tragic accident occurred: the principal bricklayer fell to his death from the scaffolding. The dedication to completing this church despite such tragedy speaks to the determination of its builders and the community they served. 8, 2002, more than 850 parishioners filled this very nave. Was at the pulpit, delivering a homily that would resonate far beyond these walls. Openly condemning Cardinal Bernard Law, he challenged the archdiocese's fundraising approach and its handling of the clergy abuse scandal. His words earned two standing ovations and captured national headlines. This moment highlighted the nave’s role not just as a place of worship but as a venue for courage and communal voice. Their absence was first noted when they failed to attend Mass here for their 50th wedding anniversary. Ahead, the altar you first explored continues the narrative of devotion and transformation.

Directions: As you exit the Nave of Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church, head towards the main entrance on Washington Street. Walk straight ahead until you reach the Portico area, located at the front entrance of the church. Enjoy the stroll and take in the beautiful architecture along the way.

Stop 3: Portico

Address: 85 Washington St, Newton, MA 02460

Coordinates: 42.3372, -71.2064

Type/Specialty: Entrance area with architectural significance

Specific Examples: Columns, archways, welcoming space

Orientation: As you step out of the nave, which you visited just moments ago, you're now facing the Portico of Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church in Newton, Massachusetts.

The portico stands as a silent witness to significant events that unfolded within this community, particularly during the tumultuous days of December 2002. During this period, H. Cuenin, a priest during the abuse scandal, took a stand against the archdiocesan leadership amid the Boston clergy sexual abuse scandal. In a bold move, he organized a meeting at the parish to challenge an archdiocesan fundraising campaign, addressing the crisis in leadership that had shaken the community to its core. Cardinal Bernard Law, who was then the Archbishop of Boston, issued a decree barring and the parish from hosting any official archdiocesan gatherings. This decree, delivered with the weight of authority, underscored the tension between the parish and the archdiocese. On December 8, 2002, the tension reached a palpable peak. Over 850 parishioners gathered in the church, filling the space you just walked through—the nave. The outpouring of support was overwhelming; Father Cuenin received two standing ovations from the parishioners, a clear testament to the community's solidarity and support for his leadership. This moment of collective defiance played a role in the eventual resignation of Cardinal Law, marking a significant shift in the archdiocese's leadership. Standing here, the portico may seem just a part of the church's exterior, but it holds the weight of these historical episodes. It is a physical reminder of the courage and unity displayed by this community. Moving forward on this tour reveals how these walls have not only witnessed acts of faith but have also been a backdrop to pivotal moments of justice and accountability.

Directions: As you leave the portico of Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church, walk along Chestnut Street. Continue on foot until you reach the entrance hall, where you'll find the stunning stained glass windows. Take your time to admire the intricate details as you stroll through the hall.

Stop 4: Stained Glass Windows

Address: 85 Washington St, Newton, MA 02460

Coordinates: 42.3372, -71.2064

Type/Specialty: Artistic glasswork depicting biblical scenes

Specific Examples: Vibrant colors, intricate designs, light filtering through glass

Orientation: As you stand in the nave, which you visited earlier, turn your gaze upward to the stained glass windows that grace the upper walls of Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church in Newton, MA. These windows, completed after years of anticipation, are a testament to both artistic beauty and community resilience.

The church, designed by James Murphy and dedicated in 1881, initially hosted its congregation in its unfinished basement, a humble beginning that underscores the deep community ties forged here. The stained glass windows, however, were not completed until much later, thanks to the persistent efforts of parishioners. These intricate windows were financed through micro-donations from local households, communities living on subsistence wages yet committed to creating a space of worship and beauty. The windows depict scenes and figures central to Catholic heritage, such as Our Lady of Perpetual Help, an important Marian devotion. Below her image are figures like Saint Alphonsus Liguori, who founded the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, reflecting themes of redemption and hope that resonated deeply with the parish's immigrant roots. In the late 20th and early 21st centuries, conservationists from John Canning & Co. embarked on a major preservation effort to restore the church's original Marian color scheme. Scientific paint and light analysis revealed how decades of soot, incense, and overpainting had dulled these vibrant colors. The restoration not only revitalized the church’s aesthetic but also rekindled its stories, ensuring that these windows continue to illuminate the lives of parishioners and visitors alike. Our Lady Help of Christians was established to serve newly arrived Irish immigrant laborers in Nonantum, providing a spiritual and cultural haven. The stained glass windows narrate tales of faith and perseverance, embodying the spirit of a community that transformed a basement gathering into a beacon of hope and beauty. As you exit, consider how these vibrant stories have shaped the streets of Newton, leaving a legacy of resilience and devotion.
